source.note: Tag names are a vocabulary index. Labels, descriptions, keywords and examples are written for Vanilla Studio.

stylized-3d.technique: Three.js meshes from code: rounded or faceted primitives, MeshPhysicalMaterial with clearcoat, soft key + rim lights. Character and prop shapes are invented, not modelled on an existing product.

sculpt-material.technique: Three.js PBR material study: procedural roughness/normal from seeded noise, transmission for translucent stone or glass, one directional key light that reveals surface relief.

diorama-miniature.technique: Small self-contained 3D set on a base; slow orbit camera; shallow depth-of-field pass; particles use a seeded generator evaluated from t.

craft-paper.technique: Layered SVG/CSS or flat 3D planes with stacked soft shadows and a fine paper-grain feTurbulence. Motion is folding, sliding and parallax, not morphing.

craft-fiber.technique: Procedural fabric: repeating SVG pattern or canvas stitches, feTurbulence fuzz on edges, small displacement. Keep stitches regular enough to read at canvas size.

line-ink.technique: SVG paths with variable stroke width and slight seeded wobble; reveal with stroke-dashoffset driven by t; paper texture through an SVG filter.

painterly.technique: Canvas 2D or fragment shader: seeded directional strokes, or feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap on flat shapes. Pre-compute stroke lists with a seed so frames stay deterministic.

print-graphic.technique: Flat CSS/SVG layers with mix-blend-mode multiply, halftone or grain patterns, and a limited ink count mapped to DESIGN.md tokens.

flat-vector.technique: Plain SVG shapes in token colors on a strict grid. Motion through transforms and shape reveals with strong easing.

cel-anime.technique: SVG or Canvas 2D characters with clean outlines and two-tone shadows; animate on twos (step t to 12 fps); painted backdrops as layered gradients. Characters are original.

collage.technique: Clipped code-drawn scraps with irregular clip-path edges, hard shadows and slight rotation. Use only licensed, user-owned images recorded in CREDITS.md.

retro-screen.technique: Render to a low-resolution buffer, then apply a post pass (scanlines, chroma offset, curvature, seeded noise keyed to frame index). Respect canvas size from workspace.json.

neon-cyber.technique: Dark token background, additive blending or CSS filter glow, bloom post pass, wet-ground reflections. Glow colors come from accent tokens.

generative.technique: Fragment shader or Canvas field: domain-warped noise, symmetry folds, curl-noise particles. Everything is a pure function of t and a fixed seed.

photo-lens.technique: Simulate a lens on code-drawn content with post passes: depth of field, grain, vignette, tone mapping. Never use generative images; real photos must be user-owned or openly licensed.

texture-surface.technique: Procedural material on type or objects: Three.js PBR maps from seeded noise, or SVG filter feSpecularLighting for 2D. Bake to a texture when the frame budget is tight.

diagram-ui.technique: Structured SVG/HTML diagram with labels from scene copy; reveal parts in order with t or step input. Text stays real text and readable.
